correctness.rationale: The claim is a finite extremal statement on source sets of at most \(19\) words. Direct deletion-shadow compatibility and an independent LCS dynamic program agree on every pair. Exhaustive subset enumeration proves the complete optimum sequence through \(n=11\), including absence of every five-word code at \(n=11\), and exactly three four-word maximizers. The packaged verifier also recomputes the published \((n,d)=(11,2)\) bound as \(823/105\).

value.rationale: The parameter is naturally selected by the source theory: \(d=2\) is the first nontrivial regime of Theorem V.2, and \(n=11\) is the first length at which the exact optimum reaches \(4\). The published upper bound rounds down only to \(7\), so the exact value and equality census close a genuine finite extremal gap and provide a compact benchmark rather than an arbitrary slice.
